description: Taxonomy of information-loss mechanisms in vector geospatial format conversion. Each code names a single, independently observable mechanism by which information present in the source is absent, altered, or unrecoverable in the target.

A1.name: Field name truncation
A1.definition: A field name is shortened to fit a target-format length limit (e.g. 10 characters in DBF).

A2.name: Field name collision after truncation
A2.definition: Two or more distinct source field names become identical after truncation and must be disambiguated or merged.

A3.name: Type coercion
A3.definition: A field is written in a different data type than the source (e.g. 64-bit integer stored as double or text; boolean stored as integer or character).

A4.name: Width or precision overflow
A4.definition: A value exceeds the target field width or decimal precision and is truncated, rounded, or rejected.

A5.name: Temporal component loss
A5.definition: Time-of-day, timezone, or sub-day resolution is dropped from a date-time value.

A6.name: Null indistinguishable from empty
A6.definition: A null value and an empty string or zero become indistinguishable in the target.

A7.name: Character encoding loss
A7.definition: Non-ASCII characters are transliterated, replaced, or mangled because the target encoding is narrower or undeclared.

A8.name: Complete attribute loss
A8.definition: All non-geometric attributes are dropped because the target format carries no attribute table.

B1.name: Z coordinate loss
B1.definition: Elevation values present in the source are absent from the target.

B2.name: M coordinate loss
B2.definition: Measure values present in the source are absent from the target.

B3.name: Ring containment loss
B3.definition: The parent-child relationship between an outer ring and its holes is not representable in the target; holes become independent geometries.

B4.name: Multipart feature split
B4.definition: A single multipart feature becomes multiple features, so feature identity and one-to-one attribute association are lost.

B5.name: Mixed geometry type coercion
B5.definition: A source containing several geometry types is forced into a single-type target, dropping or converting non-conforming geometries.

B6.name: Ring winding convention change
B6.definition: Ring orientation is reversed or normalised to satisfy the target specification.

B7.name: Empty or null geometry dropped
B7.definition: Features carrying no geometry are removed from the output.

B8.name: Invalid geometry passed or silently repaired
B8.definition: A self-intersecting or otherwise invalid ring is either written unchanged into a format that assumes validity, or geometrically altered by repair.

B9.name: Coordinate precision truncation
B9.definition: Coordinate decimal places are reduced by the writer, shifting vertex positions.

B10.name: Geometry degraded to a representative position
B10.definition: A line or area geometry is reduced to a single point, a centroid, or a bounding extent because the target carries no geometry structure. Does not apply where the writer emits a complete geometry serialisation such as WKT.

C1.name: Undeclared source CRS
C1.definition: The source carries no CRS declaration and the converter must assume one.

C2.name: Datum transformation approximation
C2.definition: A datum shift is applied using a lower-fidelity model than the authoritative one for the region (e.g. a continental three-parameter shift in place of national parameters or a grid).

C3.name: Angular units in a linear-unit target
C3.definition: Geographic coordinates are written into a format whose consumers assume linear units, producing an unusable scale.

C4.name: Axis order change
C4.definition: The order of the coordinate axes differs between source and target interpretation.

D1.name: Layer name normalisation
D1.definition: A layer or table name is altered to satisfy target character-set or length restrictions.

D2.name: Style loss
D2.definition: Symbology carried by the source (colour, line weight, icon, fill) is absent from the target.

D3.name: Hierarchy flattening
D3.definition: Nested containers (folders, groups) are collapsed into a flat list.

D4.name: Feature identifier loss
D4.definition: A stable per-feature identifier present in the source is not carried into the target.

D5.name: Label or annotation loss
D5.definition: Display names, labels, or annotation text are absent from the target.
